slice: exploring: a microbe and a body, one same-existing-society, a squid and its glowing bacteria

items.text: A disease is a landing at a between of two same-existing-societies, a body and its microbes, and is-not a trait a microbe brings: a field's damage-response framework observes the one microbe as a commensal in one body and a disease in another, Streptococcus pneumoniae and Candida albicans each living both ways, and observes a body's response too thin and a body's response too thick each landing as disease, Cryptococcus neoformans landing in one body by growing with a response too thin and in another by a response too thick to a few fungal cells; for a microbe making a toxin the framework's curve runs flat, the landing going on at any response, and a host is still its partner; pathogen, virulence, attack and defence are a field's agent story over that bi-coupling, and a self observing reads one bi-coupling, thin, middling or thick at its between.

items.section: 1.3 Every self is a same-existing-society of selves
items.text: A human body of 70 kilograms, a field's reference body, lives as some 30 trillion human cells and some 39 trillion bacteria, near one to one at about 1.3 to 1 by an approximate count, a field's older ten to one dissolving at it: a body is a same-existing-society of its own cells and its bacteria, each the other's sharing surface.

items.section: 6.7 A school, a flock, a voyaging people, an orienting surface in no self alone
items.text: A Hawaiian bobtail squid hatches with no bacteria, and from a sea full of other microbes its light organ comes to live with Aliivibrio fischeri; the bacteria sense their own density by quorum sensing, each making and sensing a small molecule, a bright glow coming at high density and a lower light at middling density; each dawn the squid vents some 90 to 95 percent of them, and the remaining tenth re-forms the society before the next night; the glow matches the light striking the squid from above and hides its silhouette from below, a squid and its bacteria orienting as one same-existing-society to a light in neither of them.

A squid and its glowing bacteria for an illustrating: bacteria glowing bright at high density, the squid venting some 90 percent at each dawn, the remaining tenth re-forming the society before the next night, the glow matching light from above and hiding the silhouette from below, one same-existing-society orienting to a light in neither of them.
